history.summary: 29-year-old (1997) freehold 3BR in Bedok/Lengkong Empat (not Geylang as the district tag implies) at $1,152 psf for a large 1,206 sqft. Absolute PSF is at the low end of the project's $1,244-1,595 range, so it screens cheap, but it is an aged, run-down, MRT-distant development with thin comps (cohort 2 txns).
history.rating_rationale: At $1,151.65 psf the unit is below the project's verified PSF range ($1,244-1,595), and a $1.39M large FH 3BR has real own-stay/family appeal — that is a genuine value angle. But the cheapness is heavily age-driven (built 1997, 'very_old_property' flag) and quality-discounted: reviews describe run-down, poorly maintained facilities, a remote location 13-14 min walk from the nearest MRT (Kembangan/Kaki Bukit/Bedok North), and small cramped units. psf_cohort_txns is only 2, so the +9.3% cohort premium and the appreciation figure are both thin. Freehold is not a forward edge per v3.4. A large old 3BR in a low-liquidity pocket is hard to exit on a 5-7yr investment horizon. Net Neutral: real but quality- and liquidity-impaired value.
red_flags: built 1997 (29 yrs) with reviews citing run-down, poorly maintained facilities
13-14 min walk to nearest MRT — no station within comfortable distance
psf_cohort_txns = 2 — cohort premium and appreciation rest on very thin data
large 1,206 sqft 3BR in a low-liquidity micro-market — slow, wide-spread exit
catalysts: Freehold large 3BR layout appeals to own-stay/family upgraders seeking space below $1.4M
Bedok/Kembangan landed-enclave amenities (Bedok Reservoir, schools) support owner-occupier demand

agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: ura_5yr_cagr 4.71% (13 txns) is the better-supported figure here, but backtest says trailing CAGR has ~0 forward power and the discount is age-driven, not a mispricing — do not extrapolate.
